briefing.headline: OpenAI deploys o4 multi-agent system as US-China AI tensions escalate

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The global AI race intensifies with frontier labs releasing advanced multi-agent systems while regulatory scrutiny grows. Compute buildouts accelerate amid supply chain constraints. Prompt injection attacks continue to dominate security discussions across production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI launches o4 with native multi-agent orchestration; Anthropic ships Claude 4 Opus; Google DeepMind releases Gemini 3; Meta open-sources Llama 4 405B variant; xAI deploys Grok-3; DeepSeek unveils R2 reasoning model. Competition centers on agentic workflows and long-context reasoning.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime monitoring for agent swarms while automotive and IoT sectors pilot protocol-level defenses.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA ships Blackwell Ultra clusters to Microsoft and Google; TSMC begins 2nm AI chip production; new hyperscale data centers announced in Texas and Arizona totaling 8GW capacity. Sovereign AI initiatives in Europe and Middle East drive additional demand.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent systems reach reliable superhuman performance before robust safety protocols are standardized across labs?
